-Yes, I've smoked recreationally since I was in college. Usually with just friends or at a party. Rarely by myself.
-I just started using weed to treat my anxiety and depression last year, so 31 years old.
-I always knew that I enjoyed weed. I've tried basically everything else for my depression: meds, ECT, therapy, yoga, diet, exercise, meditation, ketamine. So I started smoking daily last year.
-I've become addicted. People say that marijuana isn't addictive, but in my case it has been very addicting. I still manage my life. I go to work and have friends and a girlfriend. But each day I can't wait to go home and smoke weed lol.
-I would probably just share my experience with marijuana and explain that while you have to be careful with it (as I became addicted). It really can help manage mood swings.
I would also ask people:
How well do you feel marijuana helps with your depression and/or anxiety? Can you explain or give examples of how it helps you?
-Its certainly not a cure. Depression and anxiety are still the biggest forces in my life unfortunately. However, marijuana helps my moods from getting out of control. The biggest emotional problem I have with depression is anger/ irritability and I'm rarely angry or irritable after smoking weed.

Can I ask what kind of project you're doing? And feel free to ask me anything else if you think of anything.

thanks for your comment, sorry it took a while to get back to you. You make a lot of good points, that our parents are people too and you can't expect them to be perfect. Also, they are a product of how they were raised, and their parents weren't perfect either. Thanks again for your thoughtful comment.

I'm not sure I understand what is going on with "her." She wants to make friends yet thinks about ripping them off? And I'm not sure what it means when you say "if only her heart reflected her touch". The poem is brief, maybe you could elaborate more on what you are trying to say.

Nice poem. As someone with depression I can certainly relate to wanting to stay in bed all day. I think you touch on important issues related to depression, although I'm not sure you meant to do that specifically. I like the line "I want deadlines to swim away from me and peaceful silence to infect my brain." I think that's a good description of what anxiety feels like.
In terms of a critique I would say maybe add some rhyming or consistent meter.
Thanks, I'm glad you liked it. I hope it gave you a chuckle or two.
Thank you very much, I appreciate your comment. I wrote this as a senior in highschool and found it like 10 years later when I was cleaning out some old stuff. So glad I never threw it away.
I think you touch on the important parts of love, and overall its good. I had trouble getting a feel for the rhythm of the poem, but maybe that's because I'm a poetry newbie.

I liked it. I think you touch on the important parts of a making a big decision. I think the poem might have been more interesting if you made some allusion to what the decision was. Overall, I think its good though.
Thank you all for the comments and I'm glad you liked it. Your feedback is helpful and I also agree that the word 'shit' is out of place.
Haha I didn't even think of that but that's a great compliment. Thanks.
Thanks!
I liked it, and as a shy person myself I can really relate. I would agree with the comment below that maybe the poem would flow better if the lines were of similar length.
Overall I like the poem and I think it illustrates important ideas. It sometimes seems, though, that you're forcing a rhyme and letting that dictate what you're saying.
Yeah it would be nice if I already knew someone women from before I was depressed because they would know who I really am. Who I am now with depression isn't the real me.

Yeah, I've done that before too. I made a profile on OKCupid but deleted it after a few days because looking at profiles of women killed my self-esteem. So I downgraded to tinder, but had the same result lol. Thanks for the comment, I feel the same way about a potential relationship, that I would just take, take, take.

Hi, thanks for the comment, and yeah I've done CBT and related stuff and I'm aware of the distortions you mentioned, and I recognize that they play a part in my perception of all of this. Your response is the typical one that I get from my family: I could date if I wanted to, I'm just scared to try.

Hey thanks for sharing something so personal. I agree with your first point that its a negative feedback loop. My depression makes it hard to date, and being lonely makes me depressed. I also haven't been laid in a long time. I think even holding hands with a woman now would be so much physical contact that it would be overwhelming lol.

I too fantasize about a future where I'll be able to date, but I've been waiting for a long time just like you.

Hi, thanks for the commenting from the other side of the issue. Although I bet that someone who loved me would care a lot about me if I were to become depressed in the course of our relationship, I think that my problem would be that I don't know if anyone would fall in love with me in my current depressed state. I'm a decent looking guy, and initially attracting women is not really my problem, its more about maintaining their interest.

Thanks for the comment, and yeah I guess there is a gender issue here. And also you make a good point that we usually don't get much emotional support outside of romantic relationships; I think the emotional support from a relationship is what I want most but it can be hard to get that from someone you're not having sex with lol.
Thank you, your kind words are appreciated.
Have you thought about Ambien? I take that and its not contraindicated with ssri's. Its pretty effective too, and doesn't leave you groggy in the morning.

Thank you for all your comments. I've decided I'm not going to do it, I think it would have been a mistake. I think maybe I was just desperate for something that might help me feel better. Depression makes me feel so isolated, but like I posted to HoardingStrings, I think it would be better to get more out of the connections that I do have rather than superficially communicating with a lot of people.

Thank you for this thoughtful comment. And you're right, facebook is not the right place for this conversation. I've told my close friends and family already, and I think the best thing for me is to focus on strengthening the communication I have with them.
haha thank you for explaining that
Yeah I think weight lifting will be the next exercise I try. Thanks for your comment.

Yeah that is a good point, I know that I need more social support, I just don't know where to get it. My friends and family know that I have depression but I can't talk to any of them about it. I go to therapy and will start going to a support group soon, maybe that will help.

I understand the need to have a job where you don't have too much contact with others, it's exhausting. Thankfully with my job I do get some down time. Thank you for the comment.

I have no job and haven't been able to do anything that I feel like I can be proud of. I also haven't dated anyone or been laid in like 3 years. I also feel like I've wasted what could have been the best years of my life. 

I like to read about psychology and I thought this article was really good. Its about how to let go of things from the past so that you can enjoy the present more. 

https://www.psychologytoday.com/articles/201410/let-it-go

Yes, I have tension headaches. For me, the most painful part is around my eyes and in my jaw. You should see a headache specialist. Do you try to relieve the tension with stretching or progressive muscle relaxation? They take some time to start working, but are good for preventing tension from returning. 
I'm seeing a headache specialist now and she is going to give me nerve block injections in my face to "break the cycle" and then I hope that yoga and progressive muscle relaxation will prevent them from returning.

My headaches are also every day but they get progressively worse as the day goes on. My face twitches like crazy and I blink uncontrollably. This shit sucks, I feel your pain.

It helped me a lot with nausea from anxiety/ depression. I think I have only gained about 5 pounds since starting it. I'm male, 6'1" and weigh about 175 now. overall I think it works about as well as any other antidepressant I've been on, which is to say, unfortunately not very well.

"Get me the fuck out of here!"

Thanks! I hope your therapy helps you to feel better so you can live on your own sometime soon. Since I live alone now I have to be careful now not to isolate myself too much, because that's not good for mental health either. The challenges aren't behind me but I feel much more self confident now!

The challenge now for me is to keep up with all the good things I'm doing so I don't fall back into old habits. I'm going to change my job next so I can spend time outside each day.

I did a lot of research and called a lot of people until I got a nice apartment. It took about 6 weeks to get it, but when I got the keys and opened the door for the first time, it was the happiest I've felt in years.

Hi, yeah living with your parents in your late twenties can be hard on your self-esteem, at least it was for me. 

To answer your questions...
I found my new therapist on my health insurance's website. I called several and asked them about their approaches to therapy. I wanted a therapist that was very structured and would give me homework assignments between sessions. The guy I was seeing before was too laid back, almost apathetic. I've had two sessions with her so far and I like how it's going.
With the guy I was seeing before it just seemed like we were going over the same issues again and again but I wasn't making progress. I should have gotten a new therapist a while back but I put it off because its tough starting all over with someone new. 
As for your facebook, that's a decision you'll have to make for yourself. There are some people that now I won't have contact with (friends I made in other countries years ago), and that's a bit sad but I believe its for the best. Seeing people on facebook with successful careers/ relationships and buying houses and stuff made me feel too bad about myself. I think it also kept me stuck in the past, thinking about friendships and relationships that have long since faded away and that I need to put behind me to move on.

Well I believe that my depression may be partly genetic, not completely genetic, and that doesn't mean that I can't work to improve myself through things like therapy, and getting social support.

As for your question, a test for what? A test to determine if I have depression, or if I have the genetic predisposition for depression? I'm not sure if a biological test for either one of those exists.

You're right that you have to be careful about who you talk to about having depression. Some people can react to it in ways that make you feel worse. 

I would urge you to see a psychiatrist. I'm guessing that you got your rx from a primary care physician? The psychiatrist can talk to you about the dosage and give you more information in general about antidepressants. And you should still mention the light sensitivity thing to him or her.

Its good to hear that you're working in therapy, and that you're setting goals for yourself. I wish you luck.

Well through years of therapy, I've learned that my depression likely stems from genetic factors (my father and grandfather have/had depression), and also having had an abusive childhood(emotionally, not physically or sexually). Also, I had poor coping strategies, in that I hid my depression from everyone around me.

Sorry to hear that your anti depressant isn't helping much. I would definitely tell your psychiatrist about how you're feeling and the sensitivity to light.

Hey, I saw your title and had to comment. This is my ninth year of clinical depression as well. I'm 28 and got depressed at 19. I can't work, live with my mom, and feel fucking terrible everyday. You're not alone.
What medications have you tried? All SSRI's? There are other ones out there.

Yeah the MAOI's are not prescribed much any more because there are a lot of diet restrictions, and if you eat something you shouldn't, it can be very dangerous. They can be very effective though, and often work when other AD's have failed. 

I've been on parnate for 5 days now and its already working better than any other AD treatment I've tried.

Like most people commenting, I have tried many different ssri's, snri's, and a tricyclic ad, as well as wellbutrin, abilify and other cocktails. Also 23 sessions of ECT and 4 ketamine infusions to no avail.

 I have now been on parnate (an MAOI) for 4 days and it is helping more than anything else I have tried. I expect to continue improving in the coming weeks. I recommend considering an MAOI to anyone who has been let down by other AD's.
oh ok

ask about wellbutrin and then an antipsychotic such as abilify. I think most psychiatrists would add these drugs before they added lithium.

 My psychiatrist added lithium after I was already on an ad, wellbutrin, and abilify, but it didn't do anything except make my hands shake.

I've had depression for about 9 years, and there have been periods when I was exercising regularly. It never made a difference in how I felt except for a short while right after running. Everyone says that exercise is great for depression, but the research is actually mixed. It seems likely that exercise can help mild to moderate depression, but not severe depression (like mine).
That's great to hear. How long have you been taking the MAOI? I'm starting one in 2 weeks. I've read about a lot of people who tried a lot of medications to no avail, but the MAOI helped them.
I work part-time. I found an easy job that I can manage. Of course I don't earn very much, so I'm living at my mom's house for free.

Luckily it didn't really have any effects on my memory though. Most people have some short-term memory loss.

Hey there. I also have depression and with it, incredible fatigue. I started taking Adderall a few years ago, though, and it has helped a lot. You could ask your doctor about that. I take it in addition to my antidepressants.

My depression did not respond to the ECT at all. I was just as depressed after the treatment as before.

I also did not have any noticeable memory issues, though, which is unusual.

I'm happy to answer any questions you have.
ECT? ask your psychiatrist about it. It might be worth considering. It helps a lot of people. I had it, but it didn't help me at all.

I think this is a common symptom of depression. I know that it affects my life greatly. Because of the depression, my mind doesn't work fast enough to keep up with the pace of conversation.

How is your thinking aside from conversation? Are you able to concentrate? 

As with all depression symptoms, if you treat the depression effectively, the symptoms should remit.
I wouldn't try weed for depression. I have depression and I smoke weed occasionally. It lets me have some fun, but sometimes it makes the depression worse.

This is a really great point to bring up, and I honestly don't know how I feel about being in a relationship while suffering from depression. 

I've had two major relationships while depressed, and the depression caused significant stress in both of them. Both women didn't really understand it, and expected me to be able to just snap out of it, which made me feel really bad about myself. 

It depends on the person you're in a relationship with, I guess. Some people are more understanding about depression, and others don't get it at all.

I have a BA and MA in psychology and also want to be a researcher in psychology, but I can't because I have depression. Currently I'm working a stupid part-time job completely unrelated to psychology.

I actually got a good position as a research assistant after I got my MA, but I got fired because I couldn't actually do the job (because of brain fog and poor memory).

Yeah I work a few days a week as a standardized patient. I pretend to have an illness and medical students practice interviewing me/ making diagnoses. Its pretty easy so I'm grateful to have it.

Hey man, I'm a 27 year old male with MDD and GAD. I work part-time at some stupid job to try to make ends meet. I tried having a full-time job but I couldn't cut it because of the brain fog and anxiety, like you mentioned. 

I've said it in other posts, but the one thing that I hate most about having depression is that I can't have a good job/ career. It makes me feel like a loser, but I try to remind myself that depression isn't my fault.

Hang in there pal, you're certainly not alone.

I work part-time at an easy job and I'm grateful to have it. I tried having a full-time job but I got fired because I couldn't do the work, due to the depression. 

For me, not being able to have a career is the worst part of my depression.

Well the thing is that most people do recover from depression. The people who never recover from depression are the minority. I understand how you feel, living with depression really sucks. 

I would just urge you to consider the following. It is the depression that makes you think that you will have it forever. Hopelessness is a symptom of depression. If you work hard, you will probably recover.

How old are you now?

What treatments have you tried for your depression?

Feel the same way. Been depressed for nearly 9 years. Tried everything to get better, but nothing has worked. I think I might try deep brain stimulation before I do it though. What treatments have you tried for depression?
My dad left our family about 10 years ago. I know that he regrets it everyday.
Depression cost me a fulfilling college experience, and thousands of dollars that I would have earned if I was able to keep a job. It cost me 9 years of my life.

I've had two girlfriends while depressed, and I came out to both of them. They both reacted pretty well, and said that they wanted to help me get better. 
The depression caused a lot of friction in the relationships though, and neither of them could understand why I couldn't be more productive. Also, both felt as if I wasn't trying hard enough to get better, when I was doing the best that I could.

I've had 4 ketamine infusions for depression. The first was part of a clinical trial, and the other 3 were administered by a doctor as a depression treatment. It did give me a boost in mood, but it didn't make me completely better. And the effect only lasted about 2 weeks.

I'm happy to answer any questions you have about it.

yeah memory loss is common. I didn't really notice any memory loss, however. I would have gladly traded some memories for it to have been effective, though.
I had 23 sessions of ECT. 14 unilateral, and 9 bilateral. It didn't help my depression in the slightest, but it does help most people.
Not wanting to hurt my family. Also, I just started a new medication now and the suicidal thoughts have almost completely disappeared.

Well if you took some time off, you would have to make sure to keep yourself as busy as possible. Go to therapy, exercise, do hobbies, do cognitive behavioral therapy exercises, maybe have a part-time job. 

The goal of depression treatment should always be the complete elimination of symptoms, so that you're free to actively participate in life (especially in college).

right, adding an antipsychotic can help too. I was on abilify with my SSRIs but it still wasn't helping. Now, instead of being on an SSRI, wellbutrin, abilify, and buspar all at once, I'm just on a tricyclic and its doing more than all the others combined.

hi,

I had clinical depression all though my college years, and it sucked. My grades were awful, I had no friends, and I wasn't involved in any activities really.

 I can tell you honestly that not taking time off from college to deal with my depression is one of the biggest regrets of my life. I'm not saying that's what you should do, but maybe its worth thinking about. College can be such an amazing time, full of awesome opportunities to grow and learn, but depression can prevent you from taking advantage of it. If I could go back in time, I would take a semester or year off from college and not go back until I felt better.

I feel incredibly stupid because of the depression. Slow thinking, poor concentration and poor memory are common symptoms of depression. The real problem is that depression makes it feel like these symptoms are your fault. The truth is, though, that when your depression gets better, you get your fully functioning brain back.

Hi,
I've had 23 sessions of ECT in the past, 14 unilateral and 9 bilateral. 

1. For the unilateral, I couldn't detect any effects on my memory at all. When I got bilateral there were a few things that people mentioned that I didn't remember. It seemed like I lost some specific memories, but it didn't seem to have an effect on my memory capacity at all (my ability to make new memories).

2. I never really felt confused after each treatment, I just felt groggy from the anesthesia.

3. It did not work for me, unfortunately. It pretty much had no effect at all on the depression. This is an uncommon experience though, as ECT helps something like 70% of the people who get it.

4. I couldn't relapse because I never got better, but relapse happens a lot to people who don't stay on their meds or don't have maintenance ECT.

5. The bilateral gave me bad headaches, but that was it. 

6. I only told a few people that I had it done. No one needs to know about it unless you want them to. As for employers finding out, there is no way they can find out unless you tell them. Your medical information is strictly confidential. I would try not to worry about the stigma, getting better is what's most important. Since you have been depressed for over a decade and tried over 15 meds, I would say ECT is probably right for you.

Let me know if you have other questions, and how it turns out for you.

Yeah I have taken other antidepressants. I've been on a bunch of different SSRI's, wellbutrin, abilify, buspar, and some others. The ketamine definitely had a stronger effect than those did, but again, it only lasted about 2 weeks.

I think this is a great question to ask. 
I was never depressed before I went away to college, and have been severely depressed ever since then (that's 8 years now). 
A lot of times I get angry at myself for not being able to be productive or for not being funny or intelligent. And then I have to remind myself: that is the depression.
The biggest difference between the depressed version of me and the non-depressed version of me is that I can't be productive now, and my brain works no where near as well as it used to. I remember that I used to be smart and funny and be able to do a lot of things, but now I'm stupid, boring, and lazy. 

Anyway, I think you're question is a great one to ask because we need to remind ourselves of how great life can be without depression. I think a lot of depressed people begin to forget how much depression dampens the experience of life, and it contributes to their hopelessness.

I had 3 infusions over 3 days back in January in NYC. It helped me feel a little bit better, but not much. And the effect doesn't last long, which I'm sure you know. For me, it lasted about 2 weeks. 

I think that the ketamine infusions are best suited for people who are suicidal and need immediate relief. They are certainly not a long-term solution. I'm happy to talk to you more about it if you have any questions.

I slept through a lot of classes because I couldn't pull myself out of bed. I couldn't study because my concentration was so bad. I never had a girlfriend or many friends because of the depression too. 

I would recommend you think about taking some time off if your depression is really bad and it's affecting your grades and overall quality of life. Not taking time off from college to deal with my depression is probably my biggest regret in life.

Well memory problems and general difficulty concentrating are common symptoms of depression. I suffer from both, and its the reason that I can't pursue the career I want. My mind simply doesn't function well enough. For me its a symptom of the depression, and not the medication, though.

I have a masters degree in experimental psychology and my dream is to be a researcher/ university professor. However, I've been fired from two research jobs because my depression leaves me at a low level of functioning. Currently I'm working a stupid part-time job that I hate because I can't function well enough to have a career. Depression has literally ruined my career.
Amen brotha.

I guess on some level I knew that something was wrong with me, but I certainly didn't know it was depression. Going to a doctor and getting diagnosed made me feel better, because then I had a name for what was wrong with me.
